- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward drift; add 3–5% upward adjustment to prevent premature bottoming.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model tends to overcorrect; apply a 2–3 day lagged mean reversion to smooth out overshoot.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and forecast is volatile, favor smoother, lower-variance trajectories; avoid high-frequency swings.  
- In periods with strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often underestimates recovery; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average.  
- When sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., 3+ days of ±0.3 sentiment), reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term noise; use 7-day smoothing filter.
